title: 💬 Speaking Part 1 — Interview

sections.heading: What happens in Part 1
sections.body:
Part 1 lasts 4–5 minutes. The examiner introduces themselves, confirms your identity, then asks questions on 2–3 familiar topics:

• Where you live / hometown
• Work or studies
• One more topic: hobbies, food, travel, technology, sports, etc.

You will NOT be asked complex abstract questions in Part 1 — these belong in Part 3. Part 1 is about YOU and your immediate world.

sections.heading: What the examiner is assessing
sections.body:
Even in simple Part 1 questions, all four criteria are assessed:

🗣️ Fluency: Do you speak smoothly without long pauses?
📚 Vocabulary: Do you use varied, precise words?
⚡ Grammar: Do you use a range of structures?
🔊 Pronunciation: Are you clear and natural?

Your vocabulary and grammar in Part 1 SET THE TONE for your score.

highlight: The examiner makes their first impression of your language level in the first 60 seconds. A strong Part 1 opening creates a positive expectation for the rest of the test.

title: 🏠 Talking About Where You Live
body:
This is almost always asked. Prepare it thoroughly.

Band 6 answer: "I live in a city. It is quite big and busy. I like it."

Band 8 answer: "I'm currently based in Kochi, which is a coastal city in southern India — it has this fascinating blend of Portuguese colonial architecture and ultra-modern tech infrastructure, which I find quite unique. I've lived there for about six years now and I'm still discovering new things about it."

What made it Band 8:
• Specific location detail
• Interesting contrast (colonial + modern)
• Personal reflection ("I find quite unique")
• Ongoing connection ("still discovering")

quick.label: Add a personal reflection at the end

question: The examiner asks: "What do you like most about where you live?" Which answer is closest to Band 8?
options: "I like it because it is nice."
"I like my city because it has many facilities and is convenient for daily life."

"What I appreciate most is probably the proximity to the coast — there's something genuinely restorative about being able to walk to the beach after work. It keeps me grounded, even during particularly stressful periods."
"I live in a big city. It has many things. I like the transport system."
correct: "What I appreciate most is probably the proximity to the coast — there's something genuinely restorative about being able to walk to the beach after work. It keeps me grounded, even during particularly stressful periods."
explanation:
✅ Band 8 features:
• "What I appreciate most is probably..." = cleft sentence (Band 8 structure)
• "proximity to the coast" = precise noun phrase
• "genuinely restorative" = precise adjective
• "keeps me grounded" = idiomatic natural expression
• Personal meaning: explains WHY, not just WHAT

❌ Others: too vague, too short, or no personal depth

instruction: Match each Part 1 topic to the best extended answer technique:

pairs.meaning: Describe one specific aspect you find meaningful or challenging
Give a contrast or interesting fact about the place
Explain HOW and WHY, not just WHAT you do
Pick one moment that represents your typical day specifically

explanation: The key insight: specificity creates authenticity. A specific, honest answer about something ordinary ("I love the smell of coffee in the morning because it's the one moment before my day begins") outscores a vague answer about something impressive.

question: The examiner asks: "Do you prefer mornings or evenings?" What is the ideal answer length for Part 1?
options: One sentence: "I prefer mornings because they are quiet."
3–5 sentences using PREL: point, reason, example, link
correct: 3–5 sentences using PREL: point, reason, example, link
explanation:
Part 1 answers should be 3–5 sentences:
• Too short (1–2 sentences) = insufficient language evidence
• Too long (8+ sentences) = risks the examiner cutting you off and suggests poor timing

PREL gives natural structure:
Point: "I'm definitely more of a morning person."
Reason: "I find my concentration is sharpest before noon."
Example: "My most productive writing always happens before 10am."
Link: "I've gradually arranged my life around that pattern."

instruction: Build a Band 8 answer opener for "Do you enjoy cooking?"
correct: I'm actually particularly into cooking South
explanation:
Wait — this doesn't form a complete natural sentence with just these words. The key pattern to practise:

"I'm actually quite into [activity], particularly [specific aspect]..."

The words "actually" and "particularly" are natural discourse markers that make the answer sound genuine rather than rehearsed. "Quite into" is natural English — more authentic than "I enjoy cooking very much."

question: How should you handle an unexpected Part 1 question you have no opinion on?
options: Say "I don't know" and wait for the next question
Give a made-up answer with confidence
Use a thinking-time phrase, then offer a tentative opinion with hedging language
Ask the examiner to give you a different question
correct: Use a thinking-time phrase, then offer a tentative opinion with hedging language
explanation:
You will sometimes get questions you've never thought about. That's fine.

✅ "That's not something I've thought about much, actually... I suppose if I had to say, I'd lean towards... though I'm not entirely sure why."

This demonstrates:
• Natural thinking-time phrase
• Hedging: "I suppose", "I'd lean towards", "not entirely sure"
• Attempting an answer = fluency evidence

Hedged uncertain answers score better than silence or refusal.
